reason: The cited evidence does not address CoCrFeNi with Ti additions. E1 describes wear testing of CCAs but provides no data on Ti-modified CoCrFeNi or oxide glaze formation. E2 discusses a different alloy system (TiNbZrAg) and a different mechanism (amorphous-crystalline nanocomposite with Ag nanocrystals), not Ti-rich oxide glazes. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ti addition to CoCrFeNi promotes formation of a continuous Ti-rich oxide glaze during sliding
The Ti-rich oxide glaze is nanocrystalline and stable from RT to 800 °C
The oxide glaze reduces friction by 20–30% and wear by an order of magnitude
The mechanism involves Ti reacting with environmental oxygen at the sliding interface
The cited evidence supports these specific claims for CoCrFeNi with ~3 at.% Ti
